Folks — putting down some practical notes while we prepare the packet: 

- For this account: prospect indicated EU headquarters and US analytics team. They asked explicitly about EU→US meaningful transfer pathways.
- Private deployment note: they mentioned pilot in GCP-europe-west1 (need to confirm) — if they go VPC Private with EU control plane, cross-border concerns reduce.
- KV cache replication: default Redwood routing keeps KV cache local to serving region; cross-region replication only happens for explicit multi-region cache mirroring (customer opt-in). We should call out that default is no cross-border cache replication.
- Logs & retention: platform logs (request/trace metadata) retained for 90 days by default; audit logs can be retained longer under enterprise retention add-on — include options + pricing blurb.

Subject: Completed: Technical Transfer Safeguards + DPA Annex (Redwood response)

Hi Sara — attached is our completed technical questionnaire (Redwood_DPF_Response_v1.2.pdf) and a draft DPA annex (DPA_Annex_Redwood_v3.docx) for your legal team to redline. I also attached an operational dataflow diagram (dataflow-map.png) showing where customer content, KV cache, and logs reside for hosted/dedicated/private modes.

Highlights and clarifications (TL;DR):
- Transfer legal basis: We provide model inference and do not change the lawful basis you apply; for transfer safeguards we support SCCs with encryption and contractual commitments (SCC Annex included in DPA annex).
- Encryption: Data-in-transit uses TLS1.3; at-rest encryption uses customer-managed KMS for Dedicated & Private deployments. For hosted API we offer SSE with Redwood-managed keys by default and offer customer-managed KMS on request.
- KV Cache: By default, KV caches are ephemeral and bound to the serving instance; persistent KV caching across regions is only enabled with explicit customer configuration.
- Subprocessors: Appendix B in the DPA annex lists current subprocessors and subprocessors' roles; we require subprocessors to adhere to same contractual safeguards.
- Dataflow & logging: Request-level logs include request-id and tokenized metadata; customer content is not logged beyond ephemeral processing unless opt-in for analytics.

Attachments included: Redwood_DPF_Response_v1.2.pdf (completed questionnaire), DPA_Annex_Redwood_v3.docx (draft annex with SCC references), dataflow-map.png (visual).

We marked a few items in the questionnaire as "customer-choice" where configuration determines the control (e.g., KMS ownership, log retention). If you confirm pilot deployment mode (VPC in europe-west1 vs Hosted), we will mark those as final.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Privacy & Compliance Lead
